label: Streaming text
purpose: Render an answer as it streams — the leading edge marked, the settled text readable as plain prose.
when_to_use: While assistant tokens are arriving and should be shown as they land.
when_not_to_use: For a finished answer (render it as static text) or before the first token (use Thinking/TypingIndicator).
composition: The newest N words carry the brand accent, then transition to foreground
A blinking caret at the leading edge while streaming
responsive: Flows as a paragraph; wraps to its container.
accessibility: aria-live=polite + aria-busy while streaming so assistive tech follows the update
colour is emphasis only — every word settles to foreground, so meaning never rests on the accent (no-color-alone)
the whole text is shown at once under prefers-reduced-motion
anti_patterns: leaving text in the accent colour permanently — the accent marks the edge, not the content
using the accent as the only cue that text is still streaming (pair it with aria-busy + the caret)
assumptions: Streaming is SIMULATED here by a timer over a fixed string — replace with the real token stream.
`accentWords` (3) is a presentation choice; tune to the streaming rate.

references.note: assistant-ui's Elements catalogue (https://www.assistant-ui.com/elements, checked 2026-08) is the CONCEPTUAL reference; no code is copied. Atomic text element — no shadcn primitive — built from DLS tokens (foreground + the --brand accent) only.
